lines.en: Time: 4:43 AM\nLocation: Kumon-mi High\nMood: Bad
There isn’t much I remember from my youth.
Too much time has passed now.
But among the things I do remember, there’s one very specific sensation that gives me goosebumps to this day whenever I’m feeling despondent enough to recall it.
It’s spring. And starting next week, we won’t need to come to school for a while.
Today, we do, though.
The air is crisp. It’s cold, but I can handle it without a jacket. My hair is wet from the shower.
There’s a slight soreness on my right shoulder from where my backpack rests, tugging at the skin and forcing me to adjust it every thirty seconds or so.
I see someone. I recognize her.

We don’t speak, but we’ll make eye contact every once in a while, silently acknowledging each other’s existence as we stare up at a dull blue sky, reveling in the quiet, contemplative peace we can only experience now.
When college starts, we won’t need to wake up this early anymore. We can make our schedules as we see fit. And abandon these moments that, presently, we don’t yet realize we love.
One day, though, we’ll look back on those mornings before school. The crackle of fallen branches beneath our feet as the low roar of the bus finally comes within earshot.
We will long for the warmth. The fading of goosebumps as we step inside and find our seat not quite in the back, yet not quite in the front either.
It’s like things get brighter each block we travel. The sun is waking up again. My hair is still drying.
And in ten minutes, I’ll be right behind that girl I pretend to never think about, thinking about how I always wind up thinking about her.
It’s suddenly cold again. I’m outside. The moon is vanishing. My shoulder hurts once more.
And I don’t realize this is what happiness is.
Kirin Kanda didn’t normally wake up this early. And, on a technical level, that was true again today for she hadn’t woken up at all.
She was here because she couldn’t sleep. Because she’d gotten into a fight with her parents and spent the night waiting for an apology that never came and never would come.
She was cold, but she could handle it without a jacket.

And it wouldn’t be long now until the doors of the school would open and she could wait out the rest of the morning in the cafeteria, separating herself from the silence because the silence made her think.
If she dissolved into nothing right now, no one would notice at first. No one would question it.
Her parents, her friends, and her sister would all assume rebellion. And it wouldn’t be until her remains began to drift across the sea that anyone would realize something was wrong.
That’s how it always is.
But in the morning, in the cold, the world finally feels like it wants us.

Like the moon is gazing down, greeting us with the “good morning” we never get from the girl at the bus stop before following us to school. Never losing its place in the sky until we’re finally where we’re meant to be.
Even when we are, though...
Even when she is...
It all feels incorrect.
Perhaps it was all just too good to be true.
: You look larger than normal today, Mr. Moon. I take it you’ve been working out?
: Why yes, Kirin! Thank you very much for noticing!
: You don’t seem all that happy yourself, though. Are you feeling unloved again?
: A little. Do you think that’s childish of me, Mr. Moon?
: We all feel that way sometimes, Kirin. It’s not something that can be helped.
: Ever?

: That’s right! You’re destined to periodically feel this way from the moment you gain consciousness up until the moment you die! So it’s best to just learn how to deal with it now before it’s too late!
: What happens when it’s too late?
: When it’s too late, you won’t even want to get out of bed anymore! But the fact that you were able to today is proof that you have it in you to move forward!
: Keep pushing, Kirin! Find a purpose! For one day, you’ll know that all of this anguish was worth it! And that you’re just as special, if not more, than everybody else!
: You’re starting to sound like those self-help podcasts I listen to.
: Well, that’s probably because I’m the manifestation of your innermost thoughts and not actually a talking moon!
: I’m only saying these things because they’re exactly what you want to hear despite lacking the resolve to actually reach out and ask for help from a real person!
: Well, damn, Mr. Moon. Couldn’t you at least wait until it’s a little brighter outside to rain all over my parade?
: It’s the clouds who are responsible for rain, Kirin! I’m just a big, stupid space rock who follows you to school every day!
: Kirin?
: Oh. Miku. Hey.
: I wasn’t talking to the moon or anything if that’s what it looked like.
: Weird, cause that’s exactly what it looked like. The heck you doin’ here so early?
: What are you doing here so early? And in your...soccer uniform no less? The soccer club’s been disbanded for years.
: Ah...yeah. Yeah, I...know that.
: I still kind of...come here before school all the time, though. I...guess I just miss it and...stuff.
: Really? Why don’t you ever invite me? I’d come play with you.
: You ain’t ever really been a morning person, though. And I-
: Wait, yeah! You never answered my question! The heck are you doin’ here so early? Cause you ain’t in uniform, so I’m sure it ain’t about soccer.
: Oh, just...you know. Hanging out.
: Why didn’t you ask me then? This one of them “alone time” things I’m interruptin’ right now?
: Miku, it’s not even 5:00 AM yet. Why would I invite you anywhere?
: Idunno. But I don’t know why you think I should invite you to play soccer at 5:00 AM either if you ain’t gonna invite me to sit around and look sad.
: Well, we can...hang out now, I guess? I can’t really play soccer in a skirt, though.
: Not with that attitude, ya can’t.
: You doin’ okay? Cause I’m here to talk if ya need somebody, you know.
: I know you are. I’m just being stupid and immature.
: Think it’s a little more than bein’ stupid and immature if you’re out here talkin’ to the friggin’ moon.
: Okay. Then, I’m being very stupid and immature. So stupid and immature that I couldn’t sleep at all over an argument I can barely even remember.

: Which just makes me angry too so it’s a like a whole flood of shitty emotions that I can’t do anything about because they all happened in the middle of the night and nobody was awake and nobody would care anyway and it’s like a million things are happening at once and I’m just overwhelmed and I would like you to interrupt me now because I’m running out of breath!
: Hah! Hah...hah...
: Feel better?
: No.
: Maybe ya will later then. That’s how it worked for me.
: Took a bunch of sessions with my therapist for me to start feelin’ any better from talkin’ about stuff.
: Probably gonna have to start that whole process over now, though, since Maki’s makin’ me get a new one.
: What? Why?
: Somethin’ with Makoto preachin’ about the end of days or whatever.
: I don’t really get it. But we use the same person and if things ain’t workin’ for her, I’ve gotta man up and find somebody else too to show my support.
: I always forget Makoto has depression. She seems so normal most of the time.
: She’s good at hidin’ stuff. Way better than you, at least. Ain’t ever found her talkin’ to the moon. She’s normally sleepin’ like a baby when I head out in the morning too.
: It’s not like this is normal for me. Things have just been...not that great lately.
: I feel that, for sure. Pretty sure Maki’s startin’ to catch onto how Makoto and me have become semen demons. She don’t even want us talkin’ to Sensei anymore.
: Heh...Meanwhile, I keep feeling tempted to confess everything to my parents just to see how they’d react. Or if they’d even react at all when, honestly, I doubt it.
: They’ve never loved me, Miku. And I know you don’t like this subject, but I just...
: I just want to be noticed, you know? I want to be seen. And, more often than not, it feels like my entire existence does nothing but make everyone’s life worse.
: Guess that whole archery thing ain’t workin’ out for ya then, huh?
: Huh? What do you mean?
: Well, wasn’t the whole reason you didn’t follow me and Karin to the swim team so that you could “carve out your own path” or whatever?
: If you’re off doin’ your own thing and everything still feels wrong, can you really say it’s working? Are you really happy tryin’ to be different when you know you’d feel more comfortable with us?
: It beats living in your shadows at least. That was the other part of why I didn’t follow you. I could never actually compete with you or Karin.
: You think you’ll be able to compete with Uta and Touka then? Cause I heard Uta’s some kinda super archer and you just know Touka’s got her own kyudojo at home.
: Kirin...Don’t tell anybody else who was ever on the team I said this, but it’s okay to quit sometimes. Cause if you ain’t havin’ fun, what’s even the point?
: I just...want to be the best at something. Anything.
: The way I am now, I...feel disposable. Like, what makes me special?
: Who says ya gotta be special at all?
: Me! My parents! And probably a million other people too!
: Not Karin. Not Noriko. Not me. We all fell in love with you without you needin’ to do anything special.
: Well, you’re all dumb! And that still doesn’t change the fact that I can’t figure out how to be happy with myself! Not when there’s a better version of me everywhere I look!
: My parents know it! I know it! You know it! And the only person who doesn’t know it is fucking Karin because that’s just how perfect and amazing and beautiful she is!
: I want to impress her too, Miku! I don’t want to feel like a leech anymore! Because all of the love I do get just feels like pity to me! And I can’t escape that feeling no matter how hard I try!
: And I’m...sorry for yelling. It just feels like no one ever understands even when I explain myself the best I can.
: I’m tryin’...Think it’s hard to ever get how anybody’s really feeling if you ain’t feelin’ it yourself, though.
: I really do think the answer is just...running away sometimes. But where would I even go?...
: We’re trapped in here...We’re trapped in here and there’s no place for me, so why bother looking for one? Why try to be good at all? Why did I think I could do this?
: I wish I knew what to say that would help, Kirin. But all I’ve really got is that I love you.
: I love you too, Miku...
: It’d be really nice if that was enough.
: Morning, Miku! Here early again I- wait, Kirin?
: What are you doing here? You don’t wake up early.
: Morning...I-
: Kirin was talking to the moon.
: Hah. Thanks, Miku. I appreciate that.
: Aww, was she?! She used to do that when she was little!
: Every night before bed, she’d open the window and say goodnight to the rabbit on the moon because she was afraid it was lonely.
: It wasn’t really until we got Pancake that she stopped doing it or- at least I thought she stopped doing it, but apparently still does because she’s just so cute and-
: AAAAHHHH OKAY, OKAY, OKAY! NO MORE! I SUBMIT! DON’T EMBARRASS ME IN FRONT OF MIKU!
: Hey, there ain’t no need to be embarrassed! We all believe in the moon-rabbit when we’re kids. It’s that whole parold-dolia thing or whatever.
: Pareidolia.
: Yeah, that.
: Of course you’d know the word. Show-off.
: Hey, doesn’t this remind you guys of old times?
: Coming to school early...setting up for morning practice before the rest of the girls get here.
: The gradual sunrise...that metallic taste of canned coffee and how our shoulders would always get sore from carrying our bags.
: Feels like forever since all three of us stood here at once.
: These days, it’s just the Champion of Justice and Soccer...
: That nickname’s never going to stick, Miku.
: Just give it time, Kirin. It’ll stick.
: Do you guys want to...
: Maybe run a few drills or something?
: What, in our school uniforms? Since when do you do anything that constitutes rule-breaking?
: Yeah, Karin. Your spotless disciplinary record would go up in flames if somebody caught us.
: We’ve still got almost half an hour until the staff starts showing up.
: Wait, you’re actually serious?
: I feel kinda bad doin’ this without the rest of the team...But I also ain’t about to let an opportunity like this slip through my fingers!
: Kirin, go get the traffic cones! Karin, you handle the balls!
: On it!
: Heh...
: What? What’s so funny?
: Ohhhh, nothing. Nothing at all, dearest...pffft....hahah...hahahah!
: Kirin, what on earth are you laughing at?!
: Hahah! Hahahahahahah!! Hahahahahaha!!!
: Ahh, youth.
: How easy it’ll be to miss these days once they’re gone for good...
: HahahaHahahahahaHAHAHahAHAHAH!!!!
: I still don’t get what- oh. OH. Kirin! Ew! That’s disgusting! Get your mind out of the gutter!
: Come on, Karin! We can handle the balls together and let Miku get the cones!
: Sure! Right after we go to the restroom so I can wash your mouth out with soap!
Nowadays, when I visit my old bus stop, I do it alone.
That girl who lived across the street moved away.
She has a family now. Their oldest daughter is seven.
All I have is you.
